questions.question:
글 [A],[B]를 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은? [4점]
[A] Every day we watch, hear, or read interesting news. However, have you ever seriously considered whether an article is really true? Everyone likes an interesting news story but what if it is completely made up? ⓐ <u>Fake news can be very harmful in that it can make people less informed or even misled.</u> Nevertheless, there have been various fake news reports throughout history. Why have some people written such false information? Let's look into some articles thinking about the hidden motives behind them.
[B] AWFUL DISASTER — Last night, an angry group of rhinoceroses broke down the walls of the cage at the zoo and escaped. They also broke down the walls of the other wild animals' cages. These animals ran down the streets and injured hundreds of people. Twelve of the animals are still on the loose. Citizens should stay indoors until further notice. Not a single act or incident described above has taken place.
At that time, those who read the article carefully laughed out loud. ⓑ <u>Those who didn't read it to the end got really worrying.</u> ⓒ <u>Not knowing the news was false, many people panicked.</u> Some tried to escape the city while others went into the parks with guns to hunt the animals. So why did The Herald make up such news? Later, they confessed that they made it up (가) <u>so that</u> they could draw the readers' attention to the unsafe conditions at the zoo.
[C] SLAV SHOOTS A FRIEND IN ARGUMENT — Mejk Swenekafew, a Slav worker at the Columbia Coal Mine, was shot and seriously wounded by John Pecitello near the mining camp Thursday evening. The two men had an argument during a meeting. The argument led to a fight, and Pecitello shot Swenekafew twice, in the chest and leg. He is now at the hospital in critical condition. Pecitello ran away after the shooting. The police are searching for him now and are warning citizens that he is extremely dangerous.
[D] Is there anything strange about the article? Read the Slav's name backwards; it spells "we-fake-news." Who wrote this and why? The Daily Telegram published this fake article so that they could prove if The Daily News, their competitor, was stealing their articles. ⓓ <u>The Daily News published the same article about "Swenekafew" the next day and thus got caught stealing.</u> The people at The Daily News had to admit their act and were harshly criticized by the public.
[E] The two articles were special cases, but ⓔ <u>there are many "fake" news articles published every day.</u> As readers, we need to read critically and judge whether the news is real or fake.
[How to spot fake news!] CONSIDER the Source: Is it from a reliable source? Can we trust the writer? / CHECK the Date: Is it a new or an old story? Is it related to current events? / READ BEYOND the Headlines: Does the headline match the content? / FIND Supporting Sources: Do other related stories provide similar content?
choices: ① Why can fake news be harmful?
② What did the rhinoceroses do in the fake article?
③ How did the people who read the article carefully react?
④ How many people were arrested for writing the fake article?
⑤ Why did The Herald make up the news?

questions.question:
빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은? [3점]
A rich and wise father had two sons, Puru and Puneet. Before he passed away, he called his two sons to give them some last words of advice. "Listen carefully, my dear sons. Live by these words throughout your life, and you will be happy," he said. "Build a house in every city. Sleep comfortably. Enjoy your food. Lastly, spend money like a rich man —" Before he could explain himself, he passed away.
After his death, the two sons took their share of the father's wealth and settled in different cities. Five years passed. ① <u>Puru, who had been following his father's words carefully, had no money left.</u> ( ⓐ ) his brother was richer than ever. ② <u>Puru was puzzled about where he had gone wrong</u>, so he visited Puneet to find out.
Puneet welcomed Puru ( ⓑ ) open arms. That night, when the brothers sat down to chat after dinner, Puru asked the question that had been ( ⓒ ) his mind for days.
"It was our father's advice that I followed, but I am not happy. I built a house in every city. But because I could not always stay there, ③ <u>I hired people and had the house looked after.</u> Father said we should sleep comfortably and enjoy our food, so I had my bed designed by experts and my meals prepared by a great chef. He told us to spend like a rich man, so ④ <u>I bought what I wanted without worrying about money.</u> But look at me now! I am empty-handed. Did you not follow our father's wisdom? Tell me, brother, how did you get so rich?"
Puneet smiled and said, "My dear brother, I also followed our father's wisdom. But I understood it a bit differently. When he said 'build a house in every city,' I took it as having a place to stay all around the world. So I made friends in every city and I stayed at their houses when I visited those cities. Also, I slept comfortably each night because I would be tired after a hard day's work, and it did not matter if I was sleeping on a bed or on the hard floor. I ate only when I was hungry, so even a simple meal tasted great."
"Spend money like a rich man?" continued Puneet. "A rich man knows how to make money grow. So, I tried to spend money on something that would bring me back more money rather than on luxurious things. For me, it was this wisdom that our father tried to explain."
Now ⑤ <u>Puru realized how foolish had he been.</u> With this wisdom ( ⓓ ) mind, Puru started a new life.
questions.explanation: 돈이 다 떨어진 Puru와 더 부유해진 형제의 대조 → But. However도 가능하나 선지에서 제외(복수정답 차단).  [출처: 비상(김진완) L6 본문]

①~⑤ 중 어법상 옳은 것은? [4점]
Jun: Mina, you look different. ① <u>You had your hair cutting short!</u>
Mina: Yes. I'm on the swimming team now. ② <u>It was at the pool that I met my new coach.</u>
Jun: Cool! Is the training hard?
Mina: Very hard. But ③ <u>practiced every day, I got much faster than before.</u>
Jun: Wow. What are you doing these days?
Mina: I swim every morning ④ <u>so that get stronger for the contest next month.</u>
Jun: Who gave you that idea?
Mina: ⑤ <u>It was my coach which told me to swim every morning.</u>
Jun: Great. I'll come and cheer for you at the contest!

M: Like what?
W: Well, most people think goldfish are not smart. But, goldfish are actually smart.

② Why don't you buy a goldfish?
③ Can you tell me more about that?
④ How long do goldfish live?

② A: I'm so worried about my speech tomorrow. B: Don't worry. You've practiced a lot.
③ A: What would you do if you had a million dollars? B: I would buy a big house for my family.
④ A: Why the long face? B: I'm so happy because I won the contest.

questions.question:
대화의 밑줄 친 부분과 비슷한 의미의 표현은? [4점]
W: James, why are you still up? It's 11 o'clock!
M: I can't sleep because <u>I'm worried about</u> the Bookworm Competition tomorrow.
W: You've read all of the books on the list. What do you have to worry about?
M: Some of the writers' names are confusing, so I'm worried that I might not remember them.
W: Don't worry about something that hasn't happened yet. You'll do fine.
M: Thanks. I'll try not to worry so much.
questions.explanation: be worried about ≒ be nervous about(걱정하다·긴장하다).  [출처: 비상(김진완) L6 대화 (Bookworm Competition)]

questions.question:
대화 흐름상 어색한 것은? [3점]
W: What are you doing, Jinho?
M: ① <u>I'm writing a review of the movie, The Time Traveler's Wife.</u>
W: ② <u>I saw that movie, too.</u> ③ <u>It was the most boring movie I've ever seen.</u>
M: I loved it, too. Emily, what would you do if you could time travel?
W: ④ <u>I would travel to the 1940s and prevent World War II.</u> How about you?
M: I would go to the Joseon Dynasty and meet King Sejong. ⑤ <u>I'm a big fan of him.</u>
questions.explanation: 뒤에서 M이 I loved it, too.라고 하므로 Emily도 그 영화를 좋아해야 함. 원문: It's one of my favorite romantic movies.  [출처: 비상(김진완) L6 대화 (Time Traveler's Wife)]
